# Future Directions

Five concrete, falsifiable conjectures arising from the LWE development in
`Catalog/Cryptography/LWE/`. Each is stated so that a single Lean theorem (or a
single counterexample) settles it.

---

## Conjecture 1 (Sharp expansion factor is attained only at the all-ones pattern)

`RingLWEStruct.abs_negaConv_le` proves `‖f ⊛ g‖_∞ ≤ n·‖f‖_∞·‖g‖_∞` in
`ℤ[X]/(Xⁿ+1)`, and the computational evidence shows the bound is attained at
`f = g = (1,…,1)` for `n = 4`.

> **Conjecture.** For every `n ≥ 1` and every `A, B > 0`, the maximum of
> `‖f ⊛ g‖_∞` over `‖f‖_∞ ≤ A`, `‖g‖_∞ ≤ B` equals `n·A·B`, and is attained
> exactly at the sign patterns `f_i = ±A·σ(i)`, `g_j = ±B·σ(j)` with
> `σ(i) = (−1)^{⌊i/1⌋}`-type alternation determined by the target coordinate `k`.

Falsifiable: exhibit `n` and vectors attaining more than `n·A·B` (would refute
the proved bound — impossible), or attaining `n·A·B` at a pattern outside the
predicted family (refutes the "exactly" clause).

**Formal target.** `∃ f g, ∀ k, ... ∧ ∀ f g attaining, pattern` in the style of
`RingLWEStruct.abs_negaConv_le`.

## Conjecture 2 (Optimal-tolerance encodings are exactly the "antipodal" ones)

The original guess here — that the sufficient condition `4|ν| < q` of
`DualRegev.decodeBit_encodeBit_add` is also necessary — has been **refuted**: at
`q = 16` the offset `ν = -4` decodes both bits correctly although `4|ν| = q`,
because the decoding window `[q/4, 3q/4)` is half-open. The correct criterion is
now proved as `DualRegev.decodeBit_correct_iff` (the residue must lie in
`[0, q/4) ∪ [3q/4, q)`), and two further theorems settle the optimality question:
`DualRegev.noise_tolerance_le_half` (no encoder/decoder pair tolerates more than
`q/2` noise residues) and `DualRegev.dualRegev_noise_tolerance_optimal` (the
midpoint encoding attains exactly `q/2`). What remains open is the
*classification* of the optimal pairs.

> **Conjecture.** Fix `q ≥ 2`. An encoder/decoder pair `(enc, dec)` on `ℤ_q`
> attains the maximal tolerance `2·#S = q` **iff** the message gap
> `d = enc(true) − enc(false)` has *even additive order* in `ℤ_q` and the
> correctness region `S` is a transversal of the cosets `{r, r+d}` inside each
> `⟨d⟩`-orbit. In particular, if `d` has odd order `k > 1` then
> `2·#S ≤ q·(k-1)/k < q`, so optimality forces `q` even and, up to relabelling,
> the midpoint encoding.

Falsifiable by an encoder whose gap has odd order yet attains `2·#S = q`.

## Conjecture 3 (Arithmetic form of the arbitrary-modulus regularity criterion)

`LWEReduction.dotHom_surjective_iff_span_top` now proves, for an arbitrary
modulus `q`, that `a ↦ ⟨a, s⟩` is surjective **iff** the coordinates of `s`
generate the unit ideal of `ℤ_q`, and `LWEReduction.dot_fiber_card_general` then
gives exactly `q^{n-1}` preimages per value. What remains open is the purely
arithmetic reformulation of that criterion.

> **Conjecture.** For every modulus `q ≥ 1` and every `s : Fin n → ZMod q`,
> `Ideal.span (Set.range s) = ⊤` **iff**
> `Nat.gcd q (Finset.univ.gcd (fun i => (s i).val)) = 1`.

This is the arbitrary-modulus companion of
`LWEArbModulus.affine_bijective_iff_isUnit`, and would make the regularity
criterion decidable by a single `gcd` computation. The forward direction is a
divisibility argument; the converse needs a Bézout identity for the `gcd` of a
`Finset` of integers, which does not appear to be available directly.

Falsifiable by a composite `q` and a secret whose coordinate `gcd` is coprime to
`q` but which fails to generate `⊤` (or vice versa).

## Conjecture 4 (Ring-LWE noise growth is subgaussian, not worst-case linear)

`RingLWEStruct.rlweResidualNoise_bound` gives the worst-case bound
`n·B_e·B_r + B₂ + n·B_s·B₁` on the LPR decryption noise, and Conjecture 1 says
the factor `n` is attained.

> **Conjecture.** If the coefficient vectors `e, r, s, e₁` are drawn
> independently and uniformly from `{−B,…,B}`, then for every `k` and every
> `t > 0`,
> `Pr[ |(e ⊛ r)_k| ≥ t·B²·√n ] ≤ 2·exp(−t²/2)`,
> so that the *typical* noise growth is `Õ(√n)·B²` rather than `n·B²`, and the
> parameter condition in `rlwe_decrypt_correct` can be relaxed from
> `4(n B_e B_r + B₂ + n B_s B₁) < q` to `4(Õ(√n)(B_e B_r + B_s B₁) + B₂) < q`
> at the cost of an explicit failure probability.

Falsifiable by a distributional simulation exhibiting tails heavier than
subgaussian at scale `B²√n`.

**Formal target.** A Hoeffding/Azuma bound applied to the single-nonzero-entry
row structure established in `RingLWEStruct.abs_twist_row_le`.

## Conjecture 5 (The true optimal smudging distribution)

`LWEReduction.smudging_l1_eq` shows the uniform window of width `N` hides a
shift `c ≤ N` at `ℓ¹` cost exactly `2c/N`. The natural follow-up guess — that
uniform noise is optimal among all distributions supported on `N` consecutive
integers — is **false**: exact rational computation gives, for `N = 3, c = 2`,
`ℓ¹` cost `4/3` for the uniform distribution but `1` for `(1/2, 0, 1/2)`; and for
`N = 8, c = 3`, `3/4` for uniform but `2/3` for `(1/3, 0, 0, 1/3, 0, 0, 1/3, 0)`.
The mechanism: the cost decomposes over residue classes mod `c`, and mass should
be concentrated on the *longest* class.

> **Conjecture.** For all `1 ≤ c ≤ N`, the minimum of
> `∑_x |P(x) − P(x−c)|` over all probability distributions `P` supported on
> `{0, …, N−1}` equals `2 / ⌈N/c⌉`, attained by the distribution that is uniform
> on one residue class `{j, j+c, j+2c, …}` of maximal length and zero elsewhere.
> In particular uniform noise is optimal **iff** `c ∣ N`.

Falsifiable by a distribution beating `2/⌈N/c⌉` for some `(N, c)`.

**Formal target.** Lower bound: total variation along each residue class is at
least twice its maximum, and the class maxima are bounded below by
`mass_j / ⌈N/c⌉`. Upper bound: exhibit the concentrated distribution.
